questions.stem: Which of HCN (hydrocyanic acid), water (H2O), HBr (hydrobromic acid), or phenol (C6H5OH) is the strongest acid?

questions.stem: Which of H3O+ (hydronium), methane (CH4), HCl (hydrochloric acid), or HNO3 (nitric acid) is the strongest acid?

options.misconception: hydronium: it is the strongest acid that persists in water, stronger than ordinary weak acids
methane: the conjugate base methyl anion is extremely unstable, so methane is essentially nonacidic
nitric acid: its conjugate base is resonance-stabilized over three oxygens, giving a low pKa

questions.explanation: Among H3O+ (hydronium),methane (CH4),HCl (hydrochloric acid),HNO3 (nitric acid), HCl (hydrochloric acid) is the strongest acid because its conjugate base is the most stabilized, which lowers its pKa and favors proton loss.
questions.hint: The strongest acid has the lowest pKa and the most stabilized conjugate base.
